verdict.rationale: The Agent Skills spec requires every SKILL.md to have a `description` (1-1024 chars) that should state what the skill does and when to use it, as the template and PDF example show. Frontmatter can also control whether Claude or the user invokes a skill, and the runtime probe confirms the frontmatter reads back cleanly. However, the vendor says Claude loads skills when relevant, while hands-on reports and Vercel's evals concretely contradict this: the skill was never invoked in 56% of cases, and triggering is described as hit or miss, so the description does not reliably predict behavior. Missing for 10: reliable description-based activation, enforcement that the 'when' part is present (it is only a 'should'), independent corroboration that activation matches the documented triggers.
